einzeiler: Americans plan to spend a record $13.5 billion on Halloween in 2026.
kurzfassung: This episode explores the trends shaping Halloween in 2026, covering popular and non-chocolate candies, viral costumes reflecting the year's pop culture, and the massive spending on elaborate yard decorations. Food writer Kim Severson, styles editor Louis Lacerre II, and reporter Callie Holderman join host Rachel Abrams to discuss these seasonal staples.
stichpunkte: Americans are expected to spend a record $13.5 billion on Halloween, driven by costs and heavy spending on decorations.
Non-chocolate candies like Nerds Gummy Clusters, Sour Patch Kids, and Skittles Popped are surging in popularity among Gen Z.
Candy prices have risen by roughly 8% year-over-year, outpacing inflation, largely due to cacao crop failures and heat waves in West Africa.
Costume trends for 2026 include references to pop culture moments, public figures, and nostalgic throwbacks.
Home Depot's 12-foot giant skeleton, colloquially known as Skelly, remains a massive viral decoration phenomenon.
New iterations of Skelly feature advanced technology, including Bluetooth integration and live-speaking capabilities.
beschreibung:
Americans are expected to spend a record $13.5 billion on Halloween this year, according to the National Retail Federation. That includes costumes, decorations and lots of candy.
In this episode of “The Sunday Daily,” our host Rachel Abrams talks about these three tent poles of the Halloween season with reporters from across the Times newsroom.
Kim Severson, who covers food, tells us about the sour, peelable and texture-confused candy edging out longtime chocolate favorites. Louis Lucero II, an editor for style coverage, predicts the most popular costumes of the year. And Callie Holtermann, a reporter who covers style and pop culture, discusses the enduring joy of “Skelly,” the 12-foot-tall Home Depot skeleton with a cult following.
On Today’s Episode:
Kim Severson covers all aspects of food culture for The New York Times.
Louis Lucero II, an editor for style coverage for The New York Times.
Callie Holtermann, a reporter who writes about style, pop culture and Gen Z for The New York Times.
